In the 1956 era. It is said to be the era when gangsters ruled the city. Especially the name Dang Bireley, or Mr. Bancha Srisuk. According to stories from his friends and former girlfriend. Dang was an orphan who grew up in the Bireley factory alley near Wat Suthat. The terrifying image of Dang came from the movie "Dang Bireley and Young Gangsters." The content of the film was largely based on the gangster novel by Suriyan Saktaisong. But after this film was released in 1997. What happened was that it caused dissatisfaction among those still alive. Specifically, the friends of Dang Bireley. Such as Pu Krung Kasem. Toy Raberd Kuad (Bottle Bomb). Lor Saphan Khao (White Bridge). Dang's group of friends came out to reveal the truth, which was poles apart from the film. The student gangs of the 1956 era were not as severe as people think. It was just like the life of a delinquent kid, to put it simply, there was nothing good about it, but you only realize it when you are an adult with a wife and kids. Dang gradually built his name and became known because he joined the group of Pu Raberd Kuad and often had fights with kids from other areas, where the weapons carried were mostly just knives and sticks. One day, Dang Bireley had a confrontation with Pu Krung Kasem, a famous student gangster from Thonburi. Pu Krung Kasem and three friends crossed the river to buy serge fabric to make long school trousers in the Banglamphu area. With both in their prime, when Pu Krung Kasem's eyes met Dang
